requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.targets`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
## Verdict

The sources satisfy `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`. The implementation covers each obligation, the `{impl}` marking is complete, and the tests exercise the main boundaries and failure cases. I found no acknowledged gaps (no FIXME) and no unacknowledged ones.

## Implementation

- **File selection.** `rust_files` (src/rust_coverage.rs) takes the files from reference discovery and keeps those with an `.rs` extension outside `root/vendor`. Only the project-root `vendor` directory is excluded, because the check is `starts_with(root.join("vendor"))`. Reference discovery itself (`discovered_files`) supplies the other exclusions: `target`, `.git`, root `book` and root `evidence`, and disallowed paths.
- **Items covered.** `missing_function_references` parses each file with `outline::RUST_PROFILE`.
  - The Rust profile (src/outline/rust.rs `KINDS`) produces `fn` nodes for both `function_item` and `function_signature_item`. That covers methods, trait methods (including bodiless ones), nested functions, and test helpers.
  - It also produces `struct`, `enum` and `union` nodes.
  - Only those four node kinds are reported.
- **Where a reference counts.** A reference counts only through `outline.comments`, whose `owner` follows the outline-comment rules. Comments attach to the next node, or to the container for inner doc comments. A comment before a field, variant or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A comment in the body belongs to the function.
  - String and raw-string literals, enclosing `mod` and `impl` blocks, and evidence inputs are never comments of the item, so none of them count.
  - Fenced references are handled through `comment_fences`. They must be closed, and they are checked with their body.
- **Valid targets.**
  - A requirement counts.
  - A term never counts.
  - A built-in counts only if `builtin.check(kind, fenced)` accepts it, so `habeas:none` must be fenced, justified, and used with `{cite}`.
  - An example counts only if `example_references_requirement` finds a `{cite}` or `{test}` of a requirement in its text. That helper is marked `{impl}`.
  - An unknown name does not count.
- **Reporting.** `validate_rust_functions` emits `file:line: <kind> <name> has no requirement or example citation`. A read failure or parse failure becomes `file:line: cannot parse Rust source: …`. Both are also pushed to `discovery_errors`, so a parse failure is reported rather than skipped.
- **Marking.** `inspect_repository_with_progress`, `rust_files`, `validate_rust_functions`, `display_path`, `missing_function_references`, `example_references_requirement` and `OutlineNode::display_name` all carry `{impl}`. The behavior in that code is either specified by this requirement or marked as implementing another definition (`authoring.progress`, `no_requirement`, `builtin_definitions`, and so on).

## Tests

- **Unit tests in src/rust_coverage.rs.**
  - `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` covers:
    - enclosing `mod` and `impl` references not counting;
    - string and raw-string references not counting;
    - unknown requirement names;
    - references in a body;
    - a comment run across a blank line;
    - trailing comments;
    - inner doc comments binding to the container;
    - outer doc comments.
  - `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, nested functions, `{test}` helpers, and test helpers without a reference.
  - `an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement` covers examples that cite or test a requirement, orphan examples, examples that only cite another example or a term, and terms.
  - `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside` covers an attached comment, a comment before a field or an attribute, and a variant comment. It also covers missing struct, enum and union items, and a nested struct.
  - `locates_functions_after_unicode_text` covers correct line numbers after non-ASCII text.
  - `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` covers:
    - multiple files and subdirectories;
    - a parse failure being reported;
    - exclusion of `target` at any depth, `.git`, and the root `vendor`, `book` and `evidence` directories;
    - `src/vendor` and `src/book` still being checked.
- **Integration tests.**
  - `tests/references.rs` checks:
    - fenced `habeas:none`, including an inline citation, an empty justification, a wrong role, an unknown built-in, and an unclosed fence;
    - Git index versus untracked files;
    - disallowed paths;
    - vendored files outside Git.
  - `tests/commands.rs` checks that status output keeps the findings.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs` checks that a parse failure fails the batch.

## Minor observations

There is no dedicated test for a file-level `//!` doc comment, and none for `extern` blocks or items produced by macros. The first follows from the outline-comment binding rule, which has its own requirement, and the others fall outside "explicitly declared" items. I do not treat any of these as gaps.

text: :::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.targets`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} targets

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under {cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git` and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
A source item MUST choose its references for each candidate definition by this
procedure, and MAY carry several:
1. If the item is a test or test helper designed to verify the definition, it
MUST use `{test}`.
2. Otherwise, if fulfilling the definition depends on the item, it MUST use
`{impl}`. For code, this means it makes a decision, performs a check,
produces an output, or handles a case the definition specifies. For a type,
this means the definition constrains its shape: fields, variants, serialized
form, or validation.
3. Otherwise, if the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the
definition changes, it MUST use `{cite}`.
4. If the item carries no reference after applying steps 1 to 3 to every
definition, it MUST cite the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, justifying why the item
exists.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.targets`
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`
{test}`requirements.references.targets`
:::{req} no_requirement
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this only when no requirement or example applies to the item under the
> reference procedure. The citation MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST
> justify why the item exists. An item with an invariant worth checking, such as
> a cache that must not change results, needs a requirement stating that
> invariant instead. An item citing this MUST NOT implement end-user-observable
> behavior that no requirement specifies.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it. Validation MUST report an inline citation of it
or a fenced citation whose body, without comment delimiters and other
references, is empty. Whether the justification holds MUST be assessed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. `habeas status --all` MUST list
each `habeas:none` citation with its item and justification.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.targets`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
